EA01.why: Both count whole-number values between two bounds from a linear setting; here the bounds come from dividing a fixed total by an inclusive interval (they flip), so the reasoning differs. Not a template.

EA02.why: Both use linearity in a table with unequal x-steps. 365 solves for unknown entries; EA02 finds the one wrong entry and corrects it. Different asked quantity.

EA05.why: Both recover miles from a total bill made of a fixed part and a per-mile part. EA05 adds a per-day allowance that grows with the days. Same family, different structure.

EA07.why: Both have a rate that changes after a threshold (gym fee after 3 months). EA07 asks a total time, not an expression. The phone-battery context also repeats SAT-494 / ACT-203 / SAT-173.

EB01.why: Same line y = 2x + c/k against the same parabola family y = x² − 4x + (7 vs 6), the same combined quadratic x² − 6x + (const − k), the same insight (half the sum of the roots, independent of the constant), the same answer 3 and the same trap 2 (the parabola's vertex). Only the tangent point changes to the midpoint of two intersections.
Sum of the intersection x-coordinates of a line and a parabola. EB01 halves it and makes k unknown, but the Vieta step is the same.
Same line y = 2x + k meeting a parabola, where k is the unknown. The retired item asks for k at tangency, a different ask.

EB02.why: The maximum of a downward quadratic is found at the midpoint of two known inputs: −5(x + 1)(x − 7) there vs −40(p − 6)(p − 14) + 2,250 here. EB02 adds the offset and the profit context.
Equal values at two inputs give the axis. 101 gives the extreme value; EB02 has to build it.

EB04.why: Solve a rational model a/(a + k) = value for its input. EB04 does it twice and takes the difference.

EB06.why: The same 3-sided fence against a wall. ACT-092 maximizes the area; EB06 fixes the area, solves the quadratic and picks the root.

EB08.why: Both rest on the same fact: for a·bˣ the middle output is the geometric mean of its neighbours (V02's E(1) = √(50·98) = 70). EB08 strips this to just that fact with only the product given. V02 asks L(1) − E(1). That is a different asked quantity, so this is close, not a template.
The same f(x) = a·bˣ, 'a and b positive constants' stem wording, with values at two inputs.

EB09.why: Recover two constants of a transformed parent function from two points, then evaluate (exponential + b there, shifted square root here).

EB10.why: Product of the solutions read off letter coefficients (Vieta). EB10 turns this into 'which must also be a solution' (reciprocal). It is not the retired template, but it uses the same Vieta-product move.

EC02.why: The same min-per-mile pace context, including the '6 minutes 30 seconds' type of mixed-unit pace. The asked quantity (distance remaining when the other runner finishes) is new.

EC05.why: Cube edge from a volume via a cube root with rounding. EC05 adds an inequality and a round-up from a billing rule.

ED01.why: Linked rotations scale inversely with size (gears by teeth there, belt and pulleys by radius here).
Two circles linked by arc length and angle. 405 has the same angle with different arcs; ED01 has the same arc with different angles.

ED02.why: Circle geometry in the plane with a chord of length 2·(leg) and two candidate positions plus a 'least/greatest' ask.

ED03.why: A measurement tolerance carried through a transformation. Here it goes through squaring and the item asks for a range width, not an inequality.

ED04.why: Tangent line to a circle where you solve for the line's parameter. This is the retired item's template family; ACT-466 is a live twin of it. ED04 changes the unknown to the slope through the origin with an off-center circle, so it is close, not a template.
Tangent from an external point with a radius-tangent right triangle (5-12-13 there, 3-4-5 here).

ED05.why: Trig ratios written as linear expressions in a constant. 057 uses the complement relation; ED05 uses the Pythagorean identity. Different reasoning.

within_list_cues: EB01, EB02, EB07: all three hinge on 'the axis/vertex is the midpoint (half the sum) of two inputs'. Three items in one set with the same key insight; consider dropping one (EB01 is also a template of gen-03 K02).
EA06 and EA10: both are 'greatest possible' asks whose key is the smallest choice, and in both every distractor comes from omitting a subtraction and so is too large. The same choice pattern twice.
EB01 and EB10: both are Vieta (sum/product of the roots read from coefficients) in the same set.
EB03 and EB06: both are rectangle optimization/quadratic-from-geometry (perimeter under a parabola; fenced pen at a wall). Mild.
EA04 and EC02: both are two constant speeds over a common course where a gap (time vs distance) is the link. Mild.
answer_errors: EB10 choice C: the rationale does not produce r − b/a. A sign error in the sum gives b/a − r, not r − b/a. r − b/a comes from writing s − r = −b/a (a difference, not a sum). The value is fine as a distractor, but the stated error is wrong.

All keys verified correct: EA01 4, EA02 20, EA03 0.5 in (man), EA04 168, EA05 680, EA06 4.25 h, EA07 70, EA08 5.70 + 0.48b, EA09 57, EA10 1,700, EB01 3, EB02 2,890 (b = 800, c = −1,110), EB03 34, EB04 5, EB05 6, EB06 40, EB07 5/2, EB08 12, EB09 7, EB10 1/r, EC01 8.5, EC02 0.77, EC03 15,360, EC04 1,560, EC05 36, ED01 5π/3, ED02 25 (r = 39 is also valid), ED03 8, ED04 3/4, ED05 8/15. All other stated distractor errors reproduce their values.
cues_or_overdetermined: EB05: over-determined. The coefficient 120 (and the 'thousands of dollars' unit) cancels in the ratio C(80)/C(40); only p/(100 − p) matters.

EA06: the key is the least choice for a 'greatest' ask, and all three distractors fail for one shared reason (they drop a deduction, so they exceed the true limit). A student who knows the answer must be the most restrictive picks the smallest.
EA10: same pattern as EA06. The key $1,700 is the smallest and roundest choice for a 'greatest' ask, and every distractor drops or mis-signs the debt subtraction and is larger.
EB08: a shortcut makes it trivial. b = 1 (allowed, since b only has to be positive) gives a² = 144, a = 12, f(3) = 12; a = 1 gives b³ = 12 the same way. No structural insight is needed.
EC01: assuming at the outset that 6.0 and 9.5 are dropped gives 8.5 directly. The case analysis only confirms the answer, so the intended 'decide its position first' step never bites.
ED02: the 'least' ask matches the natural near-side chord (x = 8). The second case (x = −8 → 39) is never needed to get the key, so 'both positions must be considered' does not affect the answer.
EA09 (minor): the key 57 and distractor D 330 are integers, while A (−0.3) and B (29.7) are decimals. A weak roundness cue.
likely_easier_than_labeled: EA03 (medium-hard): set the two expressions equal; the slopes cancel at once. Closer to medium.
EA07 (medium): two one-step rate divisions. Easy-medium.
EB04 (medium-hard): two cross-multiplications that give linear equations, then subtract. Medium.
EB05 (medium-hard): evaluate the function twice and divide. Medium.
EB08 (hard): the b = 1 or a = 1 plug-in shortcut makes it medium.
EB09 (hard): 5 − a and 13 − a as perfect squares 1 and 9 are easy to spot by trial. Medium-hard.
EC01 (hard): the naive 'drop 6.0 and 9.5' route gives the key. Medium.
ED02 (hard): the near-side case alone gives the least r. Medium-hard.
ED03 (medium-hard): direct squaring with a calculator. Medium.
ED05 (hard): many students spot 8-15-17 and x = 11 without solving the quadratic. Medium-hard.
notes: No idea uses the over-used frame 'linear f with a disguised second point, asks f(0)'.

No idea closely mirrors a specific released official SAT item that I could identify. EB06 (barn-wall fencing with a fixed area) and EA04 (P/S-wave distance) are classic textbook setups, not official SAT items.

Generator-flagged pairs, judged independently: EB08 vs gen-05 V02 = close (same geometric-mean fact, different ask). EB01 vs ACT-300 = close, BUT EB01 is a template of gen-03 K02, which the generator did not flag.
